title: International Geophysical Year
summary: The International Geophysical Year ran from 1 July 1957 to 31 December 1958 as a worldwide scientific effort among 60 countries and 10,000 scientists. Proposed by the International Council of Scientific Unions in 1952, it covered fields from aurora and glaciology to oceanography and seismology. The United States built seven Antarctic research stations for it, and Sputnik 1 was launched in October 1957, during it.
